entities.name: PMID:25088804
observations: Population-based cohort of 4,345 San Francisco Bay Area women diagnosed with breast cancer in 1995–2008; prediagnosis recreational activity assessed for the preceding three years and mortality followed through 2009.

Neighborhood characteristics were independently associated with activity and survival: selected neighborhood conditions predicted lower likelihood of meeting activity recommendations; lower neighborhood SES predicted poorer overall survival (trend p=0.02).

Women with no recreational activity had 22% higher all-cause mortality risk than the most active women. Better breast cancer-specific survival was associated with lack of parks, especially in high-SES neighborhoods; this counterintuitive subgroup association needs cautious interpretation.

entities.name: PMID:26063477
observations: California Breast Cancer Survivorship Consortium analysis of 8,995 women found neighborhood-survival associations differed by racial/ethnic group; lower neighborhood SES was associated with higher all-cause and breast cancer-specific mortality among non-Latina white women.
